name: Norway
summary: Boundary Waters tower near Ely: a 1936 reference describes a 100 ft steel tower; the author dates the removal of the Sioux River tower and its two sisters to the late 1960s or 1970s, and most of the old tower remains on site.
design: steel lookout tower, described as 100 ft in the author's 1936 survey reference
status_note: Tower brought down; the author found most of the old structure still on site.
agency: U.S. Forest Service, Superior National Forest

access.note: Reached on foot inside the Boundary Waters wilderness; the author hiked in during summer 2009.

visit.trail_note: About a mile on foot from a seven-mile forest road south off the Echo Trail; GPS-guided bushwhacking near the site.

events.note: Author's notes cite a 1936 survey monument and describe a 100 ft steel lookout tower at Norway

Author gives the late 1960s or 1970s for the Forest Service bringing down the Sioux River tower and its two sisters; Norway is inferred to be one of the sisters, since the article names Norway and Angleworm as the other two of its three towers
